facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Two reporting differences matter more than their size suggests. From 2026-01-01 the company shows amortisation of customer relationships and trade names as an operating expense instead of cost of goods sold, and it recast only the 2025 quarterly comparatives, by USD 52 million for the first nine months; the audited FY2025 and FY2024 statements print no separate amortisation line, so gross profit and the operating expense lines do not line up across the two kinds of filing while operating profit does. facts.text: Debt and liquidity are well documented at the latest date. Three funded instruments remain: senior notes due 2029, senior notes due 2032 and a term loan due 2031, with the USD 800 million revolver, drawn USD 170 million at 2026-03-31 and USD 110 million at 2026-06-30, undrawn at 2026-09-30 and expiring on 2029-10-08. The only maintenance covenant is a first lien net leverage test of 3.00x on the revolver, applied only when more than 30% of it is used; the company says it complies but prints no ratio, and the credit agreement itself was not supplied. The 2024 annual report stated a 2.5x net leverage target through the cycle; the 2025 annual report drops the number. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case against a ready-with-limits view is that the combined business has three quarters of history, a provisional purchase price allocation and no pro forma EBITDA, which could make any leverage reading of the new group unreliable. The filings point the other way on two counts: the company recasts its 2025 quarters and discloses REV’s own contribution, and the REV goodwill estimate rose by USD 19 million in the second quarter and fell by USD 42 million in the third, from USD 1,451 million at the first quarter to USD 1,428 million at the third. G3; Missing reconciliation; MATERIAL; No EBITDA or Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation for FY2025 or FY2024; the 2026 quarterly reports reconcile only 2026 and 2025 interim periods; CP-1; CP-2; LTM Adjusted EBITDA to 2026-09-30 cannot be derived from the supplied filings; Obtain the Q4 2025 earnings release or FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 56–61

G4; Missing documents; MATERIAL; Executed credit agreement, amendments and indentures not supplied; no first lien net leverage ratio printed; guarantors are unnamed and no guarantor financial information is printed; CP-1; CP-2; CP-4 family; Covenant definitions, headroom and guarantor perimeter are not established; Obtain the executed documents listed in the exhibit index; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 84–88; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 28

G5; Conflict; MINOR; REV consideration USD 3,262 million and 48.1 million shares in the annual report versus USD 3,384 million and 47.9 million shares in the quarterly reports; goodwill estimate moves across three reports; CP-1A; CP-1; Both figures kept; the USD 122 million gap equals the printed REV debt settlement (calculation C1); State both figures with their roles; revisit when the measurement period closes; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 137; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 19

facts.text: Five differences limit comparison. Full-year EBITDA is calculated because the annual reports print none, so last-twelve-month figures mix a calculated year with printed interim figures. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case that leverage is better than 3.06x is that REV earnings are only partly in the base: nine-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 727 million exceeds EBITDA (Reported) of USD 534 million by USD 193 million of add-backs, mainly deal-related and purchase accounting items, and pro forma net sales for the nine months were USD 6,359 million against reported USD 6,169 million. The case that it is worse is that those add-backs are large and their realisation status is not stated, that FY2025 EBITDA of USD 626 million is calculated and cannot be tested against an issuer figure, and that cash interest paid is not available to test cover for 2026. A printed FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA, a pro forma EBITDA for REV or quarterly cash interest paid would settle the point. No maturity ladder is printed at 2026-09-30 and the term loan principal and scheduled amortisation are not stated, so the ladder and the debt principal reconciliation use 2025-12-31; severity medium; a ladder at the latest date would close it. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 132; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 29

The ranking of the 5% senior notes, the secured borrowings and the finance leases is not stated in any filing, so they are left out of the debt stack and the cumulative leverage of the 6.25% notes is not stated; severity medium; the indentures and credit agreement would close it. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 25–28; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 84–88

The annual statements print no separate line for amortisation of purchased intangibles, so that row is not supplied for FY2024 and FY2025; severity low; recast annual figures would close it. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 94

The Specialty Vehicles segment did not exist before the merger, so its net sales are not supplied for FY2024, FY2025 and the 2025 interim columns; severity low; no action is needed. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16

Lines printed as a dash in the filings are shown as not supplied rather than zero, including discontinued operations, other income in H1 2025, acquisitions in FY2025 and the 2025 interim periods, and share repurchases in Q1 2026; severity low; the issuer could confirm they are nil. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 94–97; 10-Q_2026-03-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-06-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 4

The annual report groups deferred taxes and customer advances inside other lines, so FY2024 and the Q1 2026 deferred tax asset are not supplied separately; severity low; the Q3 report comparative gives the FY2025 split only. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 95; 10-Q_2026-03-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 5

Cash taxes paid is not printed in any filing and the split of restricted cash is not printed in the 2026 reports, while the annual reports call restricted cash immaterial; severity low; the tax footnote supplement would close it. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 97

The pro forma row treats the October 2026 consideration as cash received because the filing states total consideration only, and the buyback authorisation and the dividend have no stated amount of use; severity low; the sale agreement terms would close it. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 33–34

No industrial versus finance split exists: the financing facilitator sits inside Corporate and Other and carries no separate debt or cash, so no matched-funding debt is separated; severity low; no action is needed. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 115

Operating leases and pension funded status are printed only in the annual reports and are not refreshed for REV, and purchase obligations are printed at 2025-12-31 only; severity low; REV lease and pension disclosures would close it. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 133; 10-K_2024-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 131

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Aerials is the weak earner and the asset under review. It supplies 30.0% of nine-month 2026 sales but only 12.3% of segment Adjusted EBITDA, at a 5.4% margin against 15.0% to 17.8% elsewhere, and its Adjusted EBITDA fell USD 31 million year on year, which the company attributes to tariff costs, unfavourable mix and inflation. Without Aerials the nine-month Adjusted EBITDA margin would be 14.5% against 11.8%, before any reallocation of corporate costs, but a sale would also remove the largest sales base, and no timetable, price or use of proceeds has been disclosed a year after the review was announced alongside the REV merger. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Cash generation covers shareholder returns, but the merger consumed the cash. facts.label: Company description and ownership
facts.text: Terex makes capital equipment in four segments: Environmental Solutions (refuse bodies, utility equipment), Materials Processing (crushing, screening, material handling), Specialty Vehicles (fire and ambulance vehicles, terminal trucks, recreational vehicles, from REV) and Aerials (aerial work platforms, telehandlers). Equipment is sold through distributors, rental companies and direct sales, so cash flow follows customer capital spending, and the installed base supports parts and service whose share of revenue is not printed. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue is cyclical and project-driven: in 2025 Aerials sales fell 14.5% on weaker demand from independent rental customers exposed to smaller, rate-sensitive projects, and Materials Processing sales fell 11.6% on macro uncertainty, high interest rates and weak European demand, while national customers and large projects drove the 2026 recovery in Aerials. The mechanism is that rental and dealer customers defer fleet purchases when rates are high, which cuts volumes and absorption; the implication is that revenue durability is average, supported by replacement demand in waste, utilities and emergency vehicles that management calls stable but that is only management language. Price-cost discipline is cited in Materials Processing, and no pass-through figure is printed, so pricing power is not established. facts.text: Rivalry is intense and varies by product: the company names no single competitor across segments, and in Aerials the primary competitors named include Oshkosh (JLG), Haulotte, JCB, Manitou and Dingli, which limits price increases and exposes margin to tariffs. facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: Over 12 to 24 months the outlook rests on REV integration, tariffs and the Aerials review. Management's 2026 outlook of USD 930 million to USD 1 billion of EBITDA implies USD 203 million to USD 273 million in the fourth quarter if it uses the Adjusted EBITDA basis, against USD 286 million in Q3, a gap that suggests the outlook is cautious or out of date, and it was not updated. Tailwinds are a USD 7.0 billion backlog, replacement demand and utility grid investment, which support revenue and deleveraging. Headwinds are tariffs, rental customers managing capital spending and absorbing delivered fleets, and higher interest on the floating term loan. Over three to five years the filings give no guidance; the structural sector tailwinds are management's view, so the medium-term view is not established. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The initiating condition is a cyclical fall in rental-company fleet purchases and infrastructure projects, as happened to Aerials in 2025 when sales fell 14.5% and production was cut. The first operational break is under-absorption and lower shipments in Aerials, Materials Processing and refuse bodies, followed by weaker orders at Specialty Vehicles and slower customer advances. Financial transmission is a lower EBITDA with margins already thin in Aerials, a working capital build that reverses the release, and less room from receivable sales; a fall of 33.4% in last-twelve-month EBITDA (Reported) would return net leverage to the 4.59x seen in March 2026 (reported net debt is used), and a smaller fall would leave it between 3.06x and 4.59x, the range of pressure this scenario implies. Liquidity would still be supported by cash and the revolver, whose test applies only above USD 240 million of drawings against a peak of USD 170 million, and no maturity falls before 2029. Management levers are suspending buybacks and dividends (USD 133 million in nine months 2026), low capex, working capital release, restructuring in Aerials and the Aerials sale. Resilience therefore appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress, with the credit effect showing as leverage and margin pressure. Observable triggers are falling backlog, Aerials margin below 5.4%, revolver usage rising and buybacks above free cash flow. Basis: calculation F6; calculation F11; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 27

facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Terex presents an adequate business profile supported by USD 1,207 million of liquidity, product and customer diversification and a share-funded REV merger, but credit quality is constrained by leverage on an unproven earnings base, weak Aerials margins and resumed shareholder returns. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow covered returns by USD 120 million yet depends on working capital and receivable sales. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on REV delivering earnings before the USD 600 million of 2029 notes approach maturity and on the Aerials outcome. The primary downside path is a rental and infrastructure downturn that compresses Aerials and group margins while REV is bedding in. Business profile against typical sector issuers is not established because no peer data were supplied. Further analysis would require pro forma EBITDA, the executed debt documents, ratings and the Aerials outcome. Top risk: leverage rising again on an unproven earnings base. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F1; calculation F7

## Request

Source readiness for Terex Corp, as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: whether the five supplied Terex filings can support Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit, and what they leave out.
## Sources

| 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended 31 December 2025 | 2026-02-13 | 0e8b6c85df8394f5b5edb3ae37a6e9f0a81438f6ac5fee410e779541dac1d53b | FY2025 audited statements, opening balances for 2026, debt, lease and litigation notes, the REV merger as a subsequent event |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_tex.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 31 March 2026 | 2026-05-01 | e23bbda658715732d1c5f2f0d864627d49d1db630b0236e210c1ec235144ffe4 | First quarter 2026 statements, first purchase accounting for REV, revolver draw at quarter end |

## Findings
### Bottom line

The five supplied Terex filings support a credit snapshot as of 2026-09-30, with limits: the REV merger of February 2026 breaks comparability with earlier periods, so creditors should not read year-on-year or LTM figures across it as like-for-like.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 9

Cash of USD 407 million, total debt of USD 2,578 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 800 million are printed for that date. Covenant headroom, LTM Adjusted EBITDA, ratings, market prices and anything dated after 2026-10-29 are not established from the supplied documents.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 24–25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 47
### Key findings

The group a lender faces today is larger and different from the one the audited annual report describes. The REV merger closed on 2026-02-02 and created a fourth segment, Specialty Vehicles. REV contributed net sales of USD 1,744 million and net income of USD 17 million from the closing date to 2026-09-30. Unaudited pro forma figures are printed only for net sales, net income and earnings per share, so no combined EBITDA or leverage can be taken from the filings.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 21–22; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 9

Two reporting differences matter more than their size suggests. From 2026-01-01 the company shows amortisation of customer relationships and trade names as an operating expense instead of cost of goods sold, and it recast only the 2025 quarterly comparatives, by USD 52 million for the first nine months; the audited FY2025 and FY2024 statements print no separate amortisation line, so gross profit and the operating expense lines do not line up across the two kinds of filing while operating profit does. The REV purchase price is also printed twice, USD 3,262 million in the annual report and USD 3,384 million in the quarterly reports, and the gap equals the USD 122 million of REV debt repaid at closing.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 94; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 137; calculation C1

Debt and liquidity are well documented at the latest date. Three funded instruments remain: senior notes due 2029, senior notes due 2032 and a term loan due 2031, with the USD 800 million revolver, drawn USD 170 million at 2026-03-31 and USD 110 million at 2026-06-30, undrawn at 2026-09-30 and expiring on 2029-10-08. The only maintenance covenant is a first lien net leverage test of 3.00x on the revolver, applied only when more than 30% of it is used; the company says it complies but prints no ratio, and the credit agreement itself was not supplied. The 2024 annual report stated a 2.5x net leverage target through the cycle; the 2025 annual report drops the number.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-06-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 24–27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2024-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 11

Claims outside the debt figure are only partly refreshed. The latest operating lease liabilities, USD 129 million, are dated 2025-12-31 before the merger, and the latest pension funded status is dated 2024-12-31. The 2026 reports add repurchase commitments with a maximum contingent liability of USD 460 million, performance, bid and specialty bonds of USD 619 million, short-term customer advances of USD 271 million, long-term customer advances of USD 176 million and receivable sales of about USD 562 million in the first nine months; none of these is inside the debt figure.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 133; 10-K_2024-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 131; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 48

Adjusted EBITDA exists only in the 2026 quarterly reports: USD 727 million for the first nine months of 2026 against USD 495 million for the same months of 2025. The annual reports print no EBITDA reconciliation, so a twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA to 2026-09-30 cannot be built from the supplied documents, and it would blend pre-merger and post-merger perimeters. The 2025 annual report does print operating profit for each 2025 quarter, including USD 137 million for the fourth quarter, and a 2026 outlook of USD 930 million to USD 1 billion of EBITDA that includes REV from closing and is not updated in the 2026 reports.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 61

After the quarter end the third-quarter report prints three events: completion on 2026-10-23 of the sale of two Specialty Vehicles businesses for about USD 33 million, a further share repurchase authorisation of up to USD 500 million in October 2026, and a USD 0.17 per share dividend payable on 2026-12-18. The latest document is dated 2026-10-29, so the period to the as-of date of 2026-11-18 is not covered.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 33–34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 53
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against a ready-with-limits view is that the combined business has three quarters of history, a provisional purchase price allocation and no pro forma EBITDA, which could make any leverage reading of the new group unreliable. The filings point the other way on two counts: the company recasts its 2025 quarters and discloses REV’s own contribution, and the REV goodwill estimate rose by USD 19 million in the second quarter and fell by USD 42 million in the third, from USD 1,451 million at the first quarter to USD 1,428 million at the third.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-06-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21

The executed credit agreement and indentures would turn the covenant and guarantor statements into testable terms, and a FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation or REV’s own annual report would allow a leverage measure on one perimeter. A larger revision of the REV accounting, or a revolver draw above 30%, would raise the weight of the covenant gap.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 84–88; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 9
### Limitations

This view concerns what the filings contain and where, not credit quality: it makes no leverage, coverage or recovery judgement, and the arithmetic it carries ties printed figures to their printed parts. Page references point to positions in the supplied text files, which flatten tables into lines, so each figure was read against its row label; they are not the filings’ printed page numbers.
The 2026 reports are unaudited and the REV accounting stays provisional until its measurement period closes, so figures that depend on it can still change.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 20

## Findings
### Bottom line

Net leverage of 3.06x at 2026-09-30 has eased from 4.59x at 2026-03-31 but remains above 2.89x at 2025-12-31, so creditors rely on REV earnings that enter the last-twelve-month base only from 2026-02-02.
Basis: calculation V5; calculation V3; calculation V2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 8

Liquidity is comfortable at USD 1,207 million, made up of USD 407 million of cash and an undrawn USD 800 million revolver, and the company reports no significant debt maturities until 2029. Interest cover on cash interest can be tested only for fiscal years, at 4.01x for FY2025, because cash interest paid is not printed for 2026.
Basis: calculation Y5; calculation X2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 47
### Leverage and debt structure

The merger was paid mostly in shares, so total debt barely moved. Total debt at carrying value was USD 2,584 million at both 2024-12-31 and 2025-12-31, USD 2,749 million at 2026-03-31 when the revolver stood at USD 170 million, and USD 2,578 million at 2026-09-30 with the revolver repaid. Cash fell from USD 772 million at year-end 2025 to USD 407 million, primarily because the merger took USD 467 million net of cash acquired, so net debt rose from USD 1,812 million to USD 2,171 million over the nine months.

Basis: calculation D2; calculation D5; calculation R2; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 95; 10-Q_2026-03-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 25

The fall in net leverage from 4.59x to 3.06x since 2026-03-31 comes mostly from the denominator: last-twelve-month EBITDA rose from USD 513 million to USD 710 million as REV earnings accumulated, while net debt fell from USD 2,357 million to USD 2,171 million. Because the base mixes a calculated FY2025 with printed interim figures and includes REV for only part of the period, the ratio is a conservative reading rather than a pro forma one.
Basis: calculation L1; calculation L3; calculation D3; calculation D5; 10-Q_2026-03-31_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46
### Coverage

Interest cover on cash interest paid was 11.42x in FY2024 and 4.01x in FY2025, the fall reflecting a full year of the acquisition debt, with interest expense of USD 177 million against USD 89 million. For 2026 only EBITDA over total interest expense is available, at 3.70x on a last-twelve-month basis at 2026-09-30 against 2.83x at 2026-03-31; interest expense includes factoring discounts and, since the merger, interest on customer advances.

Basis: calculation X1; calculation X2; calculation X3; calculation X4; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 94; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 132; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 10
### Cash generation and working capital

Operating cash flow was USD 440 million in FY2025 and issuer-defined free cash flow USD 325 million, helped by a working capital release. In the first nine months of 2026 operating cash flow was USD 338 million, against USD 235 million a year earlier, and free cash flow USD 253 million; the company reports working capital at 15.0% of annualised net sales at 2026-09-30, down from 20.8% at 2025-12-31.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 58–59; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 72–73; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 48–49
### Liquidity and funding outside debt

Liquidity at 2026-09-30 was USD 1,207 million. Letters of credit totalled USD 156 million, of which USD 149 million sit under a facility that does not reduce the revolver, so the revolver is fully available. Receivable sales of about USD 562 million in the nine months and supplier finance of USD 51 million sit outside debt, and the repurchase agreements and bonds that came with REV add contingent claims of USD 460 million and USD 619 million.
Basis: calculation Y5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 27–31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 48
### Customer advances as non-debt funding

Customer advances have become a material funding float: USD 271 million short term and USD 176 million long term at 2026-09-30, against USD 44 million and USD 20 million at 2025-12-31, largely assumed with REV, whose contract liabilities were USD 359 million at closing. They fund inventory without being debt and bear interest, USD 11 million in nine months, so a slower order book or customer refunds would turn them into cash outflows.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 10
### Subsequent events and pro forma effect

After 2026-09-30 the sale of two Specialty Vehicles businesses closed on 2026-10-23 for about USD 33 million, which would lower net debt to USD 2,138 million and net leverage to 3.01x if the consideration is received in cash; the filing does not say so. A buyback authorisation of up to USD 500 million and a dividend of USD 0.17 per share are scheduled but carry no stated effect on net debt.
Basis: calculation Q1; calculation Q2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 33–34
### Definition and data-quality risks

Five differences limit comparison. Full-year EBITDA is calculated because the annual reports print none, so last-twelve-month figures mix a calculated year with printed interim figures. Debt at 2025-12-31 is USD 2,584 million on the balance sheet, USD 2,592 million as principal and USD 2,552 million under a line labelled net debt, and the first is used. The 2026 quarterly reports move amortisation of customer relationships and trade names out of cost of goods sold, so gross profit is not comparable with the annual reports, while operating profit is. The REV purchase price is USD 3,262 million in the annual report and USD 3,384 million in the quarterly reports, and letters of credit at 2025-12-31 are USD 85 million in one set of filings and USD 50 million in another.
Basis: calculation K1; calculation K2; calculation R1; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 95; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 132; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 8
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case that leverage is better than 3.06x is that REV earnings are only partly in the base: nine-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 727 million exceeds EBITDA (Reported) of USD 534 million by USD 193 million of add-backs, mainly deal-related and purchase accounting items, and pro forma net sales for the nine months were USD 6,359 million against reported USD 6,169 million. The case that it is worse is that those add-backs are large and their realisation status is not stated, that FY2025 EBITDA of USD 626 million is calculated and cannot be tested against an issuer figure, and that cash interest paid is not available to test cover for 2026. A printed FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA, a pro forma EBITDA for REV or quarterly cash interest paid would settle the point.
Basis: calculation B2; calculation E2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46
### Limitations

The ratios rest on carrying-value debt and on EBITDA that is calculated for full years, so they compare across dates only as labelled. Last-twelve-month figures are not pro forma for REV or for the 2025 sale of the tower and rough terrain cranes businesses. Covenant headroom is not calculable: the credit agreement was not supplied and no filing prints the first lien net leverage ratio. The REV purchase accounting is provisional and the 2026 reports are unaudited.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 27

## Request

Business & governance for Terex Corp, as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: what Terex does and where it earns, who owns and controls it, the acquisitions and disposals that reshaped it, and the governance and capital-allocation behaviour that bears on creditors, taken from the five supplied filings and the source-readiness summary.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Terex's creditor risk lies in management's financial policy, not in a controlling owner: no controlling shareholder is disclosed, yet two large acquisitions since October 2024 and a new USD 500 million buyback authorisation test that policy.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-K_2024-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 34

Creditors are protected by funding mix and diversification: 83.6% of the REV consideration was paid in shares, no customer exceeds 10% of sales and the largest is below 6%. They remain exposed to an unresolved review of Aerials, which is 30.0% of nine-month 2026 sales, and to buybacks that resumed in Q3 2026.
Basis: calculation B5; calculation B1; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 49
### Key findings

No controlling owner is disclosed in the supplied filings, so creditors face a public-company board and management rather than a sponsor, and the usual tests of sponsor support or extraction do not apply. The REV merger gave former REV holders shares equal to 42.1% of those outstanding on 2026-02-10. No block holder is named in the supplied filings, and holders above 5%, board independence and related-party dealings sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied.
Basis: calculation B6; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 19; Source readiness (CP-0)

The business is more diversified by product and customer than by region, and REV has made it more North American. Four segments each carry 20.5% to 30.0% of nine-month 2026 net sales, no customer exceeds 10% and the largest is below 6%, yet North America produced 81.1% of nine-month 2026 sales against 72.3% in FY2025. The customer figures predate REV.
Basis: calculation B1; calculation B4; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 15–17

Aerials is the weak earner and the asset under review. It supplies 30.0% of nine-month 2026 sales but only 12.3% of segment Adjusted EBITDA, at a 5.4% margin against 15.0% to 17.8% elsewhere, and its Adjusted EBITDA fell USD 31 million year on year, which the company attributes to tariff costs, unfavourable mix and inflation. Without Aerials the nine-month Adjusted EBITDA margin would be 14.5% against 11.8%, before any reallocation of corporate costs, but a sale would also remove the largest sales base, and no timetable, price or use of proceeds has been disclosed a year after the review was announced alongside the REV merger.
Basis: calculation B1; calculation B3; calculation B11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 41–42; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 52

The two acquisitions were funded very differently, and REV was the more creditor-friendly one on funding mix. The Environmental Solutions Group cost USD 2,010 million in cash and was financed with USD 2,000 million of new notes and term loan plus cash on hand, while 83.6% of the REV consideration was paid in shares and the cash element was USD 548 million, including USD 122 million of REV bank debt repaid at closing. The first-quarter 2026 cash flow shows cash falling and new borrowing, but no sentence names the source of that cash.

Basis: calculation B7; calculation B5; 10-K_2024-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-K_2024-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-03-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-03-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 37

Shareholder returns are resuming while the REV purchase accounting is still provisional. Nine-month 2026 dividends of USD 58 million and buybacks of USD 75 million took 52.6% of free cash flow of USD 253 million, buybacks restarted in Q3 after none in the first half, and an October 2026 authorisation of up to USD 500 million lifts repurchase capacity to USD 610.8 million. The debt agreements restrict dividends, but their limits were not supplied.

Basis: calculation B8; calculation B9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 27

Governance and reporting are conventional and clean on the evidence available, but untestable for creditor protections. The chairman is non-executive and separate from the chief executive, the auditor gave unqualified opinions on the FY2025 statements and internal control with one critical audit matter on inventory quantities in Aerials and Materials Processing, and the 2026 reports add REV controls from closing. Related-party dealings, director independence, pay and the executed debt documents were not supplied.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 91; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 93; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 52; Source readiness (CP-0)

Management's claims on REV are not yet evidence. The second-quarter report says integration is progressing as planned and the FY2025 report says ESG integration is complete and ahead of its USD 25 million synergy commitment, but no REV synergy figure is given, the 2.5x net leverage target of the FY2024 report is no longer stated, and the 2026 outlook of USD 930 million to USD 1 billion of EBITDA predates three quarters of results.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-K_2024-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 59

Overall governance and financial-policy risk is medium. The supplied filings show no extraction, related-party payment or creditor-adverse transaction and a mostly share-funded merger, set against debt-funded growth in 2024, resumed buybacks, an open portfolio review and legal limits that cannot be tested.
Basis: calculation B5; calculation B7; calculation B8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 34
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case for a more positive view is that the REV merger was paid mostly in shares, the revolver was undrawn at 2026-09-30, no single customer dominates and no distribution is shown to have been debt-funded. Management also reports Q3 free cash flow of USD 209 million and a backlog of USD 7.0 billion, and the auditor found internal control effective at 2025-12-31. On that evidence the risk could be judged low.
Basis: calculation B5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 91

The view would worsen if the executed credit agreement shows wide capacity for restricted payments, if buybacks are funded from revolver drawings or run ahead of free cash flow, if proceeds of an Aerials sale go to shareholders rather than to debt, or if the REV purchase accounting moves materially again. It would improve if the company restates a numeric leverage target, commits sale proceeds to debt reduction or discloses covenant headroom.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2024-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 11
### Limitations

- The proxy statement was not supplied, so holders above 5%, director independence, related-party dealings and executive incentives are not established; the conclusion that no controlling owner exists rests on none being named, and a disclosed block holder would turn it into an assessment of shareholder behaviour.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 83; Source readiness (CP-0)

- The credit agreement, indentures and merger agreement were not supplied, so the legal room for dividends, buybacks, investments and asset sales is not established; the financial-policy conclusion rests on observed behaviour only and would tighten or loosen once those limits are read.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 84–87; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 27

- REV's own annual report and any split of Specialty Vehicles sales by product line were not supplied, so exposure to fire and emergency, commercial and recreational vehicles inside the 28.3% Specialty Vehicles share is not established, and the cyclicality of the enlarged business is judged at segment level only.
Basis: calculation B1; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 14; Source readiness (CP-0)

- Customer concentration, employee numbers and segment backlog are printed only for the group before REV, so the diversification conclusion rests on pre-merger customer data and may differ for the enlarged group.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 22

- The latest source is dated 2026-10-29, so any outcome of the Aerials review, buyback activity or board change between that date and 2026-11-18 is not established, and the risk level is as at the last report.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 53

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Two large acquisitions and several disposals have shaped the group since 2024. On 2024-10-08 Terex bought the Environmental Solutions Group from Dover Corporation for USD 2,010 million in cash, financed with USD 750 million of 6.25% senior notes due 2032 issued at par, a new USD 1,250 million term loan due 2031-10-08 and cash on hand; the revolver was enlarged to USD 800 million and extended to 2029-10-08 at the same time.
Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-K_2024-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-Q_2026-03-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 26

On 2025-10-29 Terex agreed to acquire REV Group, Inc. in a stock-and-cash merger, which closed on 2026-02-02 with Terex taking 100% of REV's stock. Provisional consideration is USD 3,384 million in the 2026 reports and USD 3,262 million in the FY2025 annual report: USD 2,828 million in Terex shares valued at USD 58.99 each, USD 426 million of cash at USD 8.71 per REV share, USD 122 million of REV bank debt repaid at closing and USD 8 million for converted awards. REV added USD 1,744 million of net sales and USD 17 million of net income to 2026-09-30, goodwill of USD 1,428 million was assigned to Specialty Vehicles, and the purchase accounting remains provisional.

Basis: calculation B5; calculation B10; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 137; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 21

The first-quarter 2026 cash flow shows the cash side of the REV deal: USD 467 million paid for acquisitions net of cash acquired, cash down from USD 772 million at 2025-12-31 to USD 392 million at 2026-03-31, and debt proceeds of USD 235 million against USD 70 million repaid, including a revolver drawing of USD 170 million that was undrawn again at 2026-09-30. No sentence names a funding source for the cash consideration. No new notes or term loan appear in the debt note at 2026-09-30 beyond those outstanding at 2025-12-31, so the 2024 financing for the Environmental Solutions Group is the latest new debt issue in the period; the term loan was repriced to SOFR plus 1.75% on 2025-08-12.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 95; 10-Q_2026-03-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-03-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-03-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 24–26

The tower and rough terrain crane businesses went to Raimondi Cranes SpA for USD 115 million (agreed 2025-08-06, closed 2025-10-31, pre-tax gain USD 41 million). Capacity of Texas, Inc. and Mobile Products, Inc. (LayMor), two Specialty Vehicles businesses, were held for sale at 2026-09-30 with a non-cash loss of USD 20 million and were sold on 2026-10-23 to Right Lane Industries for about USD 33 million, a subsequent event that is not in the 2026-09-30 balance sheet. A further sale of an unnamed Specialty Vehicles business in the first quarter of 2026 appears only in the reconciliation notes, with no buyer or price. A strategic review of Aerials, announced with the REV merger, has no reported outcome.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 125; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-03-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-03-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 36

After quarter end the Board authorised repurchases of up to USD 500 million more in October 2026 and declared a dividend of USD 0.17 per share payable on 2026-12-18 to holders of record on 2026-11-09.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 34

Fundamental credit for Terex Corp, as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the overall credit profile, its strongest support and its primary downside, built from the five supplied filings and the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance answers; no rating, relative value, legal or sizing view is given.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Terex's fundamental credit is adequate but unproven: net leverage eased to 3.06x at 2026-09-30 (3.01x pro forma for the sale completed on 2026-10-23) and liquidity is USD 1,207 million, yet REV earnings are only partly in the ratio and Aerials margins are weak.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

No significant debt maturities until 2029 protect creditors from a refinancing squeeze. The primary downside path is a cyclical fall in rental and infrastructure demand that compresses Aerials and equipment margins while REV integration is still unproven, pushing leverage back toward the 4.59x seen at 2026-03-31. Free cash flow of USD 253 million in nine months covered USD 133 million of shareholder returns.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F1; calculation F11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 47
### Key findings

Leverage has improved quickly but on a base that is not yet like-for-like. Net leverage fell from 4.59x at 2026-03-31 to 3.06x at 2026-09-30, with net debt of USD 2,171 million (3.01x and USD 2,138 million pro forma for the sale of two Specialty Vehicles businesses completed on 2026-10-23), but it was 2.89x at 2025-12-31 before REV, and the last-twelve-month earnings include REV only from 2026-02-02 with no pro forma EBITDA printed.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Source readiness (CP-0)

Liquidity and maturities are the main support. Company-stated liquidity was USD 1,207 million at 2026-09-30 with the USD 800 million revolver undrawn (pro forma cash after the October 2026 sale is not established), and the first principal maturity of size is the USD 600 million of 5% notes due in 2029, 23.1% of the principal ladder. The only maintenance covenant is tested above 30% revolver usage, a trigger of USD 240 million against a peak quarter-end drawing of USD 170 million.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F6; calculation F7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 47

Cash generation covers shareholder returns, but the merger consumed the cash. Free cash flow of USD 253 million in nine months 2026 was 47.4% of EBITDA (Reported), the unadjusted measure used for leverage, against 51.9% in FY2025 and 31.4% in FY2024. Dividends and buybacks took USD 133 million, leaving USD 120 million, yet net debt rose USD 359 million to USD 2,171 million (USD 2,138 million pro forma for the 2026-10-23 sale) because the REV cash price was USD 467 million.
Basis: calculation F1; calculation F2; calculation F3; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 48

Add-backs flatter Adjusted EBITDA and funding outside debt qualifies the leverage picture. Adjusted EBITDA of USD 727 million for nine months includes USD 193 million of add-backs, 26.5% of the total, mostly deal costs and purchase accounting, so the leverage ratios here use the smaller EBITDA (Reported), which is conservative. Receivables sold of about USD 562 million, customer advances of USD 447 million, supplier finance of USD 51 million and repurchase and bond commitments of USD 460 million and USD 619 million sit outside debt, so a slowdown in orders or in factoring would reach liquidity before it reaches leverage.
Basis: calculation F4; calculation F12; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30

Margin stability is the weakest material dimension. Aerials earned a 5.4% Adjusted EBITDA margin on 30.0% of nine-month sales, its FY2025 segment operating margin fell 6.2 percentage points to 5.0% from 11.2%, and the Environmental Solutions margin fell to 17.0% from 19.8% on unfavourable mix, a utilities production ramp-up and lower refuse vehicle volumes, so the group Adjusted EBITDA margin slipped to 11.8% from 12.1% even with REV added.
Basis: calculation F9; calculation F14; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 115–116; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 39–42

REV is now the largest earnings contributor and its integration is the central uncertainty, while the older businesses are well spread. Specialty Vehicles produced USD 262 million, 36.0% of group Adjusted EBITDA of USD 727 million, inside a purchase price allocation that is still provisional and with consumer recreational vehicles alongside public-service vehicles; management gives no REV synergy figure. Revenue is otherwise diversified, with no customer above 10% of sales and a USD 7.0 billion backlog at 2026-09-30.
Basis: calculation F5; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 18

Financial policy is the swing factor. Buybacks restarted in Q3 and up to USD 500 million more was authorised in October 2026, the 2.5x net leverage target of the FY2024 report is no longer stated, and legal limits on restricted payments were not supplied, so willingness to put debt reduction first cannot be shown; Business & governance rates governance and financial-policy risk as medium.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2024-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 34
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case for a more positive view is that leverage may already be lower than 3.06x: the last-twelve-month base holds REV for about eight of twelve months, Adjusted EBITDA was USD 286 million in Q3 2026 against USD 186 million a year earlier, and the 2026 outlook of USD 930 million to USD 1 billion of EBITDA, if met, would exceed the USD 710 million of EBITDA (Reported) in the ratio. With USD 1,207 million of liquidity and no maturities until 2029, the profile could then be judged strong on cash flow. The outlook dates from 2026-02-13 and has not been updated.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 59

The view would weaken if net leverage on the enlarged perimeter stays near 3.06x once a full twelve months of REV is in the base, if the Aerials margin falls below 5.4%, if buybacks outrun free cash flow or if revolver usage approaches the USD 240 million test trigger. It would strengthen if the company prints pro forma EBITDA that confirms leverage near 3x, restates a numeric leverage target or applies Aerials sale proceeds to debt.
Basis: calculation F6; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Limitations
- No pro forma EBITDA is printed for the enlarged group, so the adequate-but-unproven view could move either way once REV earnings are shown for a full twelve months.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Source readiness (CP-0)

- No agency rating, market price or peer figure was supplied, so standing against sector issuers and market access are not established and the refinancing judgement rests on the maturity profile and liquidity alone.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)
- The executed credit agreement and indentures were not supplied, so the covenant definitions, restricted-payment room and guarantor perimeter behind the liquidity conclusion are unknown.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 27; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- The sector view rests on management statements about end-market demand, with no independent industry data, so the outlook for rental, waste, utility and emergency-vehicle demand is management language only.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 59
- The financial profile uses calculated full-year EBITDA and interim figures printed by the company, so cash conversion ratios compare periods only as labelled.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Strengths and weaknesses

Liquidity and a back-ended maturity profile are the strongest support. Company-stated liquidity of USD 1,207 million and an undrawn USD 800 million revolver mean a cyclical downturn would not force a refinancing before the USD 600 million of 5% notes fall due in 2029, which are 23.1% of the ladder, and the term loan and 2032 notes fall due later, so liquidity distress inside two years would need a sustained shock to earnings and cash flow, not a maturity.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 47

Cash generation covering distributions is the second strength. Free cash flow of USD 253 million exceeded dividends and buybacks of USD 133 million by USD 120 million in nine months 2026, so shareholder returns were covered by free cash flow on the evidence available, and the working capital ratio improved to 15.0% from 23.2%, which supports further cash release but could reverse.
Basis: calculation F1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 48–49

Product and customer diversification is the third strength. Four segments each carry 20.5% to 30.0% of nine-month sales, no customer exceeds 10%, and the backlog of USD 7.0 billion gives visibility for the enlarged group, so no single end market decides debt service.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 18

A share-funded merger is the fourth strength. REV was paid 83.6% in shares, so the larger of the two acquisitions added little debt, and net debt moved by USD 359 million rather than the USD 3,384 million consideration.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F1; calculation F13

The first weakness is leverage on an unproven base. Net leverage of 3.06x (3.01x pro forma) sits above the 2.89x of 2025-12-31, includes REV earnings for only part of the period, and relies on EBITDA (Reported) because 26.5% of Adjusted EBITDA is add-backs, so lenders cannot yet test a like-for-like ratio.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F4

The second weakness is Aerials. At a 5.4% margin and 13.8% of group Adjusted EBITDA it cannot absorb a volume fall, and production cuts, unfavourable customer mix and tariffs cut its FY2025 operating margin by 6.2 percentage points, which makes group margin stability the weakest dimension.
Basis: calculation F5; calculation F9; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 41–42

The third weakness is dependence on REV. Specialty Vehicles supplies 36.0% of group Adjusted EBITDA inside provisional purchase accounting and brings customer advances and dealer repurchase commitments, so integration slippage would hit earnings and liquidity together.
Basis: calculation F5; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1)

The fourth weakness is financial policy. Resumed buybacks, a new authorisation of up to USD 500 million and a leverage target that is no longer numeric weaken the anchor creditors can hold management to while legal limits are untested.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-K_2024-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 11

The fifth weakness is interest burden. EBITDA over interest expense fell to 3.54x in FY2025 from 6.80x in FY2024 and was 3.70x on a last-twelve-month basis, and the floating-rate term loan means each 100 bp adds about USD 12.27 million of interest before any hedge.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 29

### Source gate and readiness

Module status is Ready with Limitations. All five filings, Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance are in the run for 2026-11-18 and agree on the entity, the 2026-09-30 balance sheet date and the REV perimeter break, but no ratings, market prices, peer data, executed debt documents or pro forma EBITDA were supplied. The datapoints used from Financial foundation are net debt of USD 2,171 million (USD 2,138 million pro forma for the 2026-10-23 sale), net leverage of 3.06x (3.01x pro forma), liquidity of USD 1,207 million and EBITDA (Reported) of USD 710 million for the last twelve months.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Company description and ownership

Terex makes capital equipment in four segments: Environmental Solutions (refuse bodies, utility equipment), Materials Processing (crushing, screening, material handling), Specialty Vehicles (fire and ambulance vehicles, terminal trucks, recreational vehicles, from REV) and Aerials (aerial work platforms, telehandlers). Equipment is sold through distributors, rental companies and direct sales, so cash flow follows customer capital spending, and the installed base supports parts and service whose share of revenue is not printed. The acquisitions of the Environmental Solutions Group in October 2024 and REV in February 2026 moved the mix toward waste, utilities and emergency vehicles that management describes as less cyclical, which supports cash-flow visibility if the claim holds.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-K_2024-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 11

Terex is listed, with no controlling holder named in the supplied filings, so there is no sponsor whose support or extraction must be judged; creditors depend on a board with a non-executive chairman and on the debt documents, which were not supplied. Business & governance rates governance and financial-policy risk as medium.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is cyclical and project-driven: in 2025 Aerials sales fell 14.5% on weaker demand from independent rental customers exposed to smaller, rate-sensitive projects, and Materials Processing sales fell 11.6% on macro uncertainty, high interest rates and weak European demand, while national customers and large projects drove the 2026 recovery in Aerials. The mechanism is that rental and dealer customers defer fleet purchases when rates are high, which cuts volumes and absorption; the implication is that revenue durability is average, supported by replacement demand in waste, utilities and emergency vehicles that management calls stable but that is only management language. Price-cost discipline is cited in Materials Processing, and no pass-through figure is printed, so pricing power is not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 39; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Margins are the weakest dimension. Group Adjusted EBITDA margin was 11.8% for nine months 2026 against 12.1%, operating margin fell to 4.7% from 8.2% mainly on purchase accounting, and Aerials earned 5.4%, so a volume fall with under-absorbed plants would hit Aerials first. Management cites cost-out actions, a plant closure in Aerials and the Terex Operating System, and gross profit margin was 17.6% for nine months 2026 against 20.8% on mix and the REV addition, but fixed versus variable cost is not split in the filings, so operating leverage cannot be sized.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 42; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Capital intensity and cash conversion

Capital intensity is low: capital expenditure was USD 90 million in nine months 2026 and USD 118 million in FY2025, so most EBITDA can reach cash, and conversion to free cash flow was 31.4%, 51.9% and 47.4% of EBITDA (Reported) in FY2024, FY2025 and nine months 2026. The 2025 and 2026 figures were helped by a working capital release, from 24.0% of sales at 2024-12-31 to 20.8% a year later and 15.0% at 2026-09-30, and by about USD 562 million of receivables sold in nine months 2026, so a reversal would cut cash conversion; capex is the main lever, with dividends and buybacks of USD 133 million the next. REV transaction costs of USD 19 million in nine months 2026 are another claim on cash, and cash interest paid is not printed for 2026.

Basis: calculation F3; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 48
### Competitive forces

Rivalry is intense and varies by product: the company names no single competitor across segments, and in Aerials the primary competitors named include Oshkosh (JLG), Haulotte, JCB, Manitou and Dingli, which limits price increases and exposes margin to tariffs. Buyer power is high because national rental companies buy a material part of Aerials and Environmental Solutions output and customer consolidation increases pricing pressure, while supplier consolidation limits sources for some parts. Substitution risk and the threat of new entry are not established from the filings, so the credit effect is margin pressure from the largest buyers rather than a loss of volume.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 41; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Macro and policy factors

Tariffs and interest rates are material. Higher tariff costs cut Aerials nine-month Adjusted EBITDA, USD 40 million of tariff refunds were recognised in nine months 2026 and further claims await customs review, and high interest rates weigh on rent-to-own conversions and smaller projects, so policy shifts move margins and fleet purchases. Government infrastructure funding and municipal budgets support Aerials, Materials Processing and emergency vehicles, which is management's view only. Other social and technology factors do not appear to be primary credit drivers on the supplied materials.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 35
### Credit-translated SWOT

Strengths are USD 1,207 million of liquidity, distant maturities, share-funded REV consideration and low capital intensity, which keep debt service secure through a mid-cycle slowdown. Weaknesses are leverage on an unproven base, Aerials margin and dependence on REV, which cap the profile at adequate. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are demonstrated REV synergies, an Aerials sale applied to debt and continued working capital release. Threats are a rental and infrastructure downturn, tariffs, resumed buybacks and a customer-advance reversal.
Basis: calculation F5; calculation F7; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Financial profile and credit quality

Scale and market position are average: net sales of USD 7,487 million over the last twelve months give shock absorption, but no market share is printed. Competitive advantage is average, with brands and distribution but no evidence of pricing power. Business diversification is average, strong by product and customer but with 81.1% of nine-month sales in North America. Cost and capex flexibility is average, with low capex but unsplit fixed costs. Margin stability is weak, as set out above. Free cash flow stability is average, positive in each period but dependent on working capital and receivable sales. Ability to refinance is average, with no maturities until 2029 but no ratings or market data. Liquidity is strong at USD 1,207 million. Financial policy and governance is average, with medium risk in Business & governance. The trend is improving leverage on a larger base, constrained by add-backs, tariffs and the missing pro forma EBITDA.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F3; calculation F5
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over 12 to 24 months the outlook rests on REV integration, tariffs and the Aerials review. Management's 2026 outlook of USD 930 million to USD 1 billion of EBITDA implies USD 203 million to USD 273 million in the fourth quarter if it uses the Adjusted EBITDA basis, against USD 286 million in Q3, a gap that suggests the outlook is cautious or out of date, and it was not updated. Tailwinds are a USD 7.0 billion backlog, replacement demand and utility grid investment, which support revenue and deleveraging. Headwinds are tariffs, rental customers managing capital spending and absorbing delivered fleets, and higher interest on the floating term loan. Over three to five years the filings give no guidance; the structural sector tailwinds are management's view, so the medium-term view is not established.
Basis: calculation F10; 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 39
### Downside scenario

The initiating condition is a cyclical fall in rental-company fleet purchases and infrastructure projects, as happened to Aerials in 2025 when sales fell 14.5% and production was cut. The first operational break is under-absorption and lower shipments in Aerials, Materials Processing and refuse bodies, followed by weaker orders at Specialty Vehicles and slower customer advances. Financial transmission is a lower EBITDA with margins already thin in Aerials, a working capital build that reverses the release, and less room from receivable sales; a fall of 33.4% in last-twelve-month EBITDA (Reported) would return net leverage to the 4.59x seen in March 2026 (reported net debt is used), and a smaller fall would leave it between 3.06x and 4.59x, the range of pressure this scenario implies. Liquidity would still be supported by cash and the revolver, whose test applies only above USD 240 million of drawings against a peak of USD 170 million, and no maturity falls before 2029. Management levers are suspending buybacks and dividends (USD 133 million in nine months 2026), low capex, working capital release, restructuring in Aerials and the Aerials sale. Resilience therefore appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress, with the credit effect showing as leverage and margin pressure. Observable triggers are falling backlog, Aerials margin below 5.4%, revolver usage rising and buybacks above free cash flow.
Basis: calculation F6; calculation F11; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_tex.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tex.htm.jsonl, page 27
### Overall credit view

Overall, Terex presents an adequate business profile supported by USD 1,207 million of liquidity, product and customer diversification and a share-funded REV merger, but credit quality is constrained by leverage on an unproven earnings base, weak Aerials margins and resumed shareholder returns. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow covered returns by USD 120 million yet depends on working capital and receivable sales. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on REV delivering earnings before the USD 600 million of 2029 notes approach maturity and on the Aerials outcome. The primary downside path is a rental and infrastructure downturn that compresses Aerials and group margins while REV is bedding in. Business profile against typical sector issuers is not established because no peer data were supplied. Further analysis would require pro forma EBITDA, the executed debt documents, ratings and the Aerials outcome. Top risk: leverage rising again on an unproven earnings base.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F1; calculation F7
